text: Urgent. Tunnel between the 19 mine face and the loading bay has caved in. I am the shift lead. We were changing crews at 4 when the support on section B gave way and the roof came down over about ten meters. Twelve miners are on the far side of the cave-in. We can hear them knocking on the pipe so at least some of them are alive, and their air line is still connected as far as we can tell because the pressure gauge on our side has not dropped. Nobody on our side is hurt. We have tried the radio on channel 3 and channel 5, nothing. The company office says they are sending someone but that was 40 minutes ago. We need heavy lifting gear, timber for shoring, and the rescue team from the upper levels if there still is one. Please pass this to whoever runs the network on level 19. We are not leaving.

I want to report the water on level 35. Since the pumps restarted yesterday afternoon the water from the taps in the south dorms has been cloudy and it smells like rotten eggs and something chemical. A lot of people boiled it and drank it anyway because there is nothing else, the ration trucks did not come on Monday. Now four people in my corridor have bad stomach cramps and diarrhea, two of them are kids, 6 and 9, and one is an old man who lives alone, and they all drank from the same tap. Nobody is hurt but everyone is scared. I put up a sign saying don't drink from the south taps but people tear it down because the Directorate notice says the water is certified safe. We need someone to test the water and bring clean water and maybe medicine for the kids. I can show where the tap is. It is next to the laundry on corridor S-3.

Missing person. Name: Dario Vance, 34 years old, tall, short dark hair, scar on his left eyebrow, was wearing grey work overalls with the hydroponics badge. He works in the hydroponics farm on level 14 and left for his shift at 6 yesterday morning. He never came home and he didn't show up at the farm, his supervisor called me at 10 to ask where he was. One person missing, that's Dario. He has a heart condition and takes medicine twice a day and he didn't take his evening pills with him. His phone goes straight to voicemail. The checkpoint between 13 and 14 was closed for a few hours yesterday because of the protest, so maybe he tried another way down. If anyone has seen him please check in with his name or send a message to this hub. His sister is waiting at the farm entrance.

The heat exchangers on level 30 failed yesterday and the dorms are like an oven. The thermometer in our room says 41 degrees and it has been over 38 all night. Eight people in our row are elderly and they can't go up to the cooler levels because the stairs are too much for them and the lift is reserved. Nobody is hurt but two of them are dizzy and one has stopped eating. We are wetting towels and fanning them but the water is warm too. The maintenance office says the parts have to come from level 2 and there is no transport. If anyone has fans, ice, or a way to move old people up a few levels, please come. We are in row D, near the laundry, door 30-112.

Quick report but it's not an emergency yet. On level 5, in the main stairwell between the market and the school, there is a crack in the wall that has been there for years but in the last two days it got much wider, I can fit my fingers in it now, and this morning small bits of concrete were falling from the ceiling near the landing. Nobody is hurt and people are still using the stairs because it's the only way down to the market since the lift broke. I put a chair there to make people walk on the other side. I'm worried it will come down when it's crowded at lunch time. Can someone who knows about buildings come and look at it before something happens? The stairwell is next to the old post office, you can't miss it, there's a mural of a whale on the wall.

Message from the school on level 12. I am one of the teachers. This morning around 9 the ventilation fans in the east wing went quiet and nobody noticed at first because the kids were loud. Then we smelled something like burnt rubber and the air got heavy. We moved most of the classes to the gym which still has air moving, but five children are still in the library at the end of the east hallway with the librarian because she has asthma and could not walk that far fast. There is smoke in that hallway now, not thick but you can see it near the ceiling, and our eyes are stinging. Nobody is injured as far as we know. We wet some cloths and gave them out. The building manager's number goes to voicemail and the Directorate notice board still says all systems normal, which is not true. We need someone to check the fans and help us get the library group out safely. We have 140 kids in the gym and we are trying to keep everyone calm.

Hello, we are a group sheltering in storage hall 29-B. There was a fire somewhere on level 29 in the night, we don't know where exactly, and the smoke came into the dorms so we all moved into the storage hall because it has a heavy door. Nine of us are in here now, including a baby and two old men. The door is shut and we put wet blankets under it but smoke is still getting in through the vents in the ceiling and it is getting harder to breathe. Nobody is burned or injured but the baby is coughing a lot and one of the old men is very pale. We don't know if the fire is still burning or if it is safe to go out. There is no alarm sounding, which is strange. Our phones show the hub network but not the Directorate network. Please tell us if it is safe to leave and which way to go, or send someone to get us out. Hall 29-B, the door with the yellow stripe.

Explosion at the generator room on level 39 maybe ten minutes ago, I don't know what caused it. The whole corridor shook and the back wall of the generator room came down. Seven of us were in the break room next door and we got out into the corridor. Three are injured: one has burns on his face and hands, one has a broken arm I think, it's bent wrong, and one woman has a deep cut on her leg that we tied with a belt. The others are okay, just coughing from the dust. The emergency lights are on but the main lights are off. There is a smell of fuel and we are worried about another explosion so we moved further down toward the stairs. We have no medic and no stretcher. Our supervisor is not answering. Please send medics and someone who can check the fuel lines before anyone goes back in. We are at the stairwell at the north end of 39, by the blue door.

Hello, I don't really know if anyone is reading this but please, we really need help. My name is Ana and I live with my family in the east block. It has been a very long night and nobody has slept. The pumps stopped working about two hours ago, maybe a bit more, and nobody came to fix them even though we called the maintenance office at 11 and again at midnight. Now the water is rising on level 38 and it is already up to our knees in the corridor. Three kids are trapped in the pump room because the door jammed when the power flickered. Two of the adults who tried to open it are hurt, one cut his hand badly on the metal and the other twisted her ankle in the water. We have tried calling the Directorate line many times but it just rings and rings. Our neighbours on the next corridor say the same thing is happening there too, and some of them have moved their old people up the stairs already. Please send anyone who can open a jammed door and anyone with medical supplies, bandages, anything. We are scared and the water keeps coming. Thank you, thank you, please hurry.

This is about my two children, Leo and Mira, who are 7 and 10. They went to the level 8 community hall for the afternoon program at 2 and they were supposed to come home at 5. It is now 9 at night and they are not home. The hall is closed and dark and the volunteer who runs the program does not answer her phone. Two kids missing. Leo was wearing a green jacket with a broken zipper and Mira has a yellow backpack with a cat on it. They know our flat number and they know not to go below level 10 alone. I have asked the neighbours and walked the corridors on 8 and 9 twice. The checkpoint guard said he did not see them but he only started his shift at 6. Please, if anyone has seen them, check in with their names, or tell me where they are. I will be at the hall entrance all night.

Water main burst on level 37, south corridor, around 7. The water is shooting out of the wall at waist height and the corridor is already flooded to the ankles and it's getting deeper. Two people are trapped in the lift between 36 and 37, the lift stopped when the power tripped and the water is running down the shaft onto the lift roof. They are talking to us through the door and they are not hurt but they are scared and the water is dripping in on them. We tried the manual release but it won't move. Everyone else on the corridor has moved to the north end. The valve to shut the main is in a locked utility room, room 37-14, and we don't have the key, the building office is closed until morning. We need someone with the key or a tool to break the lock, and someone who can open the lift doors from the outside. This needs to happen before the water reaches the lift motor.

There was a stampede at the ration gate on level 36 about an hour ago. Someone shouted that the rations were running out and everyone pushed forward at once. Four people are injured that we know of: an old woman who was knocked down and can't stand up, she thinks her hip is broken, a boy with a bleeding head, a man with a crushed hand from the gate, and a woman who fainted and hit her face. They are all lying in the corridor next to the gate because there is no clinic open on 36. Some neighbours brought blankets. The guards closed the gate and left. There were maybe 200 people in the line, most of them have gone home now. We need medics and stretchers, and somebody to tell people that the rations will come tomorrow, because people are saying they will come back at 5 and it will happen again.

Please read this. We are the families in the deepest row of level 40, by the old sump. For three days we have been telling the Directorate office that the sump was making a grinding noise and they said it was scheduled for maintenance next week. Tonight it overflowed. The water came in under the doors very fast and now it is above the first step of the ladder. Six of us are stuck on the top bunks in unit 7 because the ladder up to the walkway is under water and slippery and my grandmother cannot climb it. Nobody is hurt yet but the water is cold and still rising, slower than before but still rising. We can hear the pump motor screaming somewhere behind the wall. The lights went out about 15 minutes ago so we are using phone lights and we do not have much battery left, I am at 22 percent. If you can see this please send a boat, a rope, people, anything, and tell them it is unit 7 at the very bottom of 40, the row past the red door.

This is Tomas from the market corridor. I'm writing this fast because my hands are shaking. About twenty minutes ago there was a huge noise, like thunder but inside the walls, and part of the ceiling came down near stall 14. Dust everywhere, you can barely see. We are on level 31, the west end where the old tram stop used to be. Two people are stuck under the rubble, a woman who sells bread and her son, I think he is maybe 16 or 17. Both of them are bleeding, we can hear them answering when we shout so they are alive. We moved some of the smaller pieces but the big beam is too heavy and every time we touch it more dust falls, so we stopped because we are afraid the rest will come down. There are maybe 30 or 40 people standing around and nobody knows what to do. The lights are still on at least. We need people with jacks or bars and someone who knows about medicine. Please tell whoever is in charge. Please.

We are three workers in the coolant plant on level 33. A coolant line burst in the turbine hall about half an hour ago and the room filled with steam. We got out into the control room and closed the door but the temperature in here keeps climbing, the wall thermometer says 47 and it was 30 when we came in. One of us got burned on the arm by the steam, it's red and blistering, about the size of my hand. The door to the stairs is on the other side of the turbine hall so we cannot get out without going through the steam. The emergency shutoff valve is in the hall too. We have water bottles, two, and a first aid box with burn gel that is mostly empty. Please send someone with protective suits who can reach the shutoff valve or open the back service hatch from outside. Hatch number is 33-C. We are okay for now but we will not be okay for long in this heat.

Writing for my neighbour who doesn't have a phone. She is an elderly woman in flat 1604 on level 16, she lives alone. She has diabetes and she ran out of insulin three days ago because the pharmacy on 16 has been empty since the blackout. This morning she was confused and sweating and shaking and she didn't know what day it was, and her daughter who usually visits on Sundays has not been able to get through the checkpoint. We gave her some sugar water and juice and she got a little better but I don't know what to do next and I'm afraid of doing the wrong thing. She has a medical card somewhere in a drawer but we couldn't find it. Is there anyone with insulin, or a nurse who can come and look at her? I am in 1606 next door and I can open her door for whoever comes. Thank you to whoever runs this network, it's the only thing that works.

Report from the level 24 shelter. About fifteen people here are sick since yesterday evening, all with vomiting and diarrhea and some with fever. The shelter has been using water from the old cistern on 24 because the pipes have been dry since Sunday. The water was brown but we filtered it through cloth and boiled most of it, but I think some people drank it without boiling because the stove ran out of gas at night. Nobody is injured, it's all sickness. We have 80 people in the shelter and we are trying to keep the sick ones in one corner but there is not much room. We need clean water, oral rehydration salts, and someone to tell us if the cistern is safe at all. The Directorate health notice says there are zero cases of water sickness this week. That is not true, there are fifteen in this room alone.

Big problem on level 32. The drainage tunnel under the east housing block has backed up and dirty water is coming up through the floor drains in every flat on the ground row. It started at about 3 this afternoon and now it is over the ankles in most flats and rising slowly. Around twenty people live on that row, lots of families with small kids, and they are moving their things up onto beds and tables. Nobody is hurt. The water smells very bad, like sewage, and we are worried about kids touching it. The Directorate maintenance line said a crew would come within 48 hours. We can't wait 48 hours. We need pumps or someone to clear the drainage tunnel, and somewhere for the families to sleep tonight. The east block is the one with the broken clock over the entrance.

Power has been out on level 22 since early this morning, maybe 5 or 6 hours now. It's not just the lights, it's everything: the fridges, the air movers, the elevator. The clinic here is running on a small generator for the medicine fridge only, and the nurse says she has fuel until about 8 tonight and then the insulin and the vaccines will start to go bad. A lot of old people live on 22 because it used to be the quiet level and many of them are stuck in their flats without the elevator. Some neighbours are carrying food up and down the stairs. Nobody has reported an injury yet but it is getting cold and dark in the corridors and someone is going to fall. The Directorate board says there is no outage on 22, which is a lie, anyone can come and see. We need fuel for the clinic generator first, and then someone to look at the main breaker.

Hi, sorry to message so late. My dad works the night shift at the level 27 checkpoint. About an hour ago a fight started in the line, something about the ration cards being wrong again, and a guard pushed people back and my dad fell and hit his head on the barrier. One man is injured, that's my dad, he is conscious but he keeps asking the same questions over and over and he threw up once. His friend from work brought him home to our flat because the clinic on 27 has been closed since Tuesday. He is lying on the sofa now. He has no medical card because they took them all for re-registration. He takes pills for his blood pressure, I don't know which ones, the box says 10 mg. We don't want to make it worse by moving him again. Is there any medic who can come to us? We are in block F, door 312. I will keep watching him and keep him awake like the internet says.
